blocks.content: Latitude is the angular distance of a point on the Earth's surface, measured in degrees north or south from the Equator at the center of the Earth.

rows: Direct overhead sun at least once a year; maximum heat year-round
Sun rays are never directly overhead; moderate temperatures and distinct seasonal changes
Sun stays low near the horizon with extreme slanting rays; extremely cold climates

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Latitudes are imaginary angular distances measured in degrees north or south from the center of the Earth.
The Equator (0°) is the largest parallel of latitude and divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
The Torrid Zone lies between the Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) and Tropic of Capricorn (23.5° S), receiving maximum solar radiation.
The Temperate Zones extend from 23.5° to 66.5° in both hemispheres, characterized by moderate temperatures and distinct seasons.
Parallels of latitude decrease in circumference from the Equator toward the poles, converging to points at 90° N and 90° S.
The Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
Distance between any two consecutive parallels of latitude is approximately 111 km across the globe.
Mahi River is the only river in India that crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.
Indira Point, the southernmost tip of Indian territory, is located at 6°45' N latitude in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
